I have the test description: It sets a variable d to an array {"a", "b"} and verifies that the XPath expression "$d = 'a'" evaluates to true, which means the expression should iterate over the variable components. The bug report states that instead of iterating the components of the variable (the array), the immediate content (the string array object itself) is compared directly, so the test fails.

The test snippet itself is:

```java
public void testIterateVariable() throws Exception {
    assertXPathValue(context, "$d = 'a'", Boolean.TRUE);
}
```

The report implies that when evaluating "$d = 'a'", the evaluation code compares the entire array to 'a' instead of checking if any element equals 'a'. So the array equality check is done incorrectly.

The method org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.InfoSetUtil.booleanValue(Object) appears to be used to convert results to booleans during evaluation, but this seems unrelated to the equality comparison.

I suspect the problematic code is in the equality comparison logic for variables, probably in a method handling the evaluation of expressions where the left-hand side is a variable. Possibly the VariablePointer or a method involved in Variable evaluation is doing the wrong equality check.

I want to see the class or method that handles equality for variables or evaluates variable expressions (e.g., VariablePointer or something in the compiler).

I will now check the signature org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.Variable.equals(Object) or methods in VariablePointer related to equality or comparison.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
